AI prototype — Youth Charter AI strategy project

Teaching an AI assistant when to stop coaching and start escalating

A working Claude-based tool built to rehearse Social Coaches through real scenarios — and to recognise the one moment it should never try to coach its way through.

My role  AI Data-Strategy Analyst, team of 6 Context  LSE × Practera consulting project, 2026 Built with  Claude

The problem

Youth Charter's Social Coaches mentor young people through difficult, real situations, but had no low-stakes way to rehearse those moments before facing them. Any AI tool built to help with this carried an obvious risk: generic or hallucinated advice in a context where the stakes are a child's safety, not a quiz score.

What it does

  1. 1

    Coach selects a real scenarioDrawn directly from Youth Charter's own documented case work, not invented material.

  2. 2

    AI reflects before it respondsIt states what it understood from the coach's answer first, so a misreading can be corrected before any feedback is given.

  3. 3

    Feedback stays groundedEvery piece of feedback ties back to the specific principle that scenario is built around — never generic coaching advice.

Except when it shouldn't coach at all. If a coach's response describes a genuine safeguarding concern, the tool stops offering feedback entirely and tells the coach to escalate to their supervisor immediately. That override was deliberately tested, not assumed.

Evidence

Both scenarios below were run against the live prototype.

What this showed me

The hard part was never the happy path — a tool that gives reasonable feedback on a reasonable answer is a fairly standard prompting exercise. The real test was the override: making sure the one scenario where coaching would be the wrong response reliably stopped the tool rather than its default instinct to be helpful. Getting that right taught me that responsible AI design isn't a layer added after the useful part is built — the safeguard has to be as deliberately engineered as the feature itself.

Scope, team and limitations

This was built as part of a six-person team project; I worked as AI Data-Strategy Analyst across the wider AI adoption strategy, and contributed directly to this prototype's scenario design and testing alongside our two prototype leads. The safeguarding override shown here was tested deliberately, including the case in Fig. 1.

Honestly, it's a prototype, not a product: it currently only runs inside a Claude session rather than behind a public link, which would need a backend to hold API access privately. Only four scenarios have been tested — wider use by real coaches would surface edge cases this version hasn't met yet.

Mira Börekçi — built as part of an AI adoption strategy for Youth Charter, a UK sports-for-development charity.
